chunks: Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

If you purchase goods in which there is measuring or weighing, then do not sell them until you take possession of them, unless you appoint someone over it. But if there is in it neither measuring nor weighing, then sell it.

key_terms.تُوَلِّيَهُ: appoint someone over it or transfer it in that manner

ai.seo_question: Can purchased goods be sold before taking possession of them in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on selling purchased goods before taking possession. Goods that require measure or weight should not be sold before qabd (possession), while goods not requiring measure or weight may be sold.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3772 - Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Abdillah (as) who said:

"If you purchase goods that require measuring or weighing, do not sell them until you take possession of them - unless you appoint someone to take possession on your behalf.
However, if the goods do not require measuring or weighing, then you may sell them immediately."
